keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «오늘날 쓸 수 있는 공룡 DNA는 남아 있지 않다(근거)» 와 «진짜 공룡을 되살리는 것은 거의 불가능하고, 최근 멸종한 동물을 되살리는 일은 가능하지만 논란이 크다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the reason (no usable dinosaur DNA remains today) and the conclusion (bringing back real dinosaurs is almost certainly impossible, while bringing back recently extinct animals is possible but highly debated). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: Whether extinct animals can be brought back

boxes.qen: Why can dinosaurs not come back?

qs.q: Why do scientists plan to edit the DNA of Asian elephants?
qs.qko: 과학자들은 왜 아시아코끼리의 DNA를 편집하려고 하나요?
opts: Because Asian elephants are close relatives of mammoths
Because elephant DNA never breaks down
Because Asian elephants are a kind of dinosaur
evs: Mammoths survived until about 4,000 years ago, and some of their DNA has been found in frozen remains.
Scientists hope to edit the DNA of Asian elephants, their close relatives, to create cold-resistant animals that look like mammoths.
Supporters say this could help protect endangered species and even restore damaged ecosystems.
The problem is that DNA breaks down over time.
why: 아시아코끼리는 매머드의 가까운 친척이에요. 그래서 그 DNA를 편집해 추위에 강하고 매머드처럼 생긴 동물을 만들려는 거예요.
Asian elephants are close relatives of mammoths, so scientists hope to edit their DNA to create mammoth-like animals.

qs.q: In the text, what does 'de-extinction' mean?
opts: Bringing back animals that have died out
Protecting animals that are still alive
evs: DNA is the set of instructions inside every cell that tells a living thing how to grow.
Some researchers are trying to bring back features of animals that disappeared much more recently, such as the woolly mammoth.
Some also argue that the money would be better spent protecting species that are still alive.
The last non-bird dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago.
why: 바로 다음 문장에서 사라진 동물의 특징을 되살리려는 연구를 설명해요. 멸종한 동물을 다시 살려 내는 일이라는 뜻이에요.
The next sentence describes trying to bring back features of animals that disappeared. It means bringing extinct animals back.

qs.q: Why is it almost impossible to bring back real dinosaurs?
qs.qko: 진짜 공룡을 되살리는 것은 왜 거의 불가능한가요?
opts: Because dinosaurs were too big to fit in a laboratory
Because no dinosaur bones have ever been found
Because readable DNA lasts only a few million years, but dinosaurs died out 66 million years ago
evs: Studies of ancient bones suggest that even in ideal, frozen conditions, readable DNA probably cannot survive for more than a few million years.
Supporters say this could help protect endangered species and even restore damaged ecosystems.
The last non-bird dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago.
Millions of people left the theater wondering the same thing.
why: 읽을 수 있는 DNA는 길어야 수백만 년밖에 버티지 못하는데, 공룡은 약 6,600만 년 전에 사라졌어요. 두 사실을 합치면 쓸 수 있는 공룡 DNA가 남아 있을 수 없어요.
Readable DNA survives only a few million years, but the last non-bird dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago. Together, these show no usable DNA remains.

ends: How do scientists find and read DNA in frozen mammoth remains?
과학자들은 얼어붙은 매머드 유해에서 DNA를 어떻게 찾아 읽을까?
Why are birds called living dinosaurs?
새는 왜 «살아 있는 공룡» 이라고 불릴까?

write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write what we should do and the result you want in English.

write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «so that» 뒤에 «누가 + 무엇을 할 수 있게» 를 넣어 목적을 분명하게 써 보세요. (예: so that bees can find enough flowers)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «so that», write who + what they can do to make the purpose clear. (e.g. so that bees can find enough flowers)
